leads.title: Arcolo Hackensack LLC, et al. v. City of Hackensack / Hackensack Planning Board (Former Sears Site Eminent Domain Challenge)
leads.why: WebSearch-only sourcing (Daily Voice/AOL, bylined Cecilia Levine, syndicated to Yahoo) reports that four related property-owning LLCs -- Arcolo Hackensack LLC, Sugensteve Hackensack LLC, Sugencole Hackensack LLC and Sugengran Hackensack LLC -- sued the City of Hackensack, NJ and its Planning Board in Bergen County Superior Court on Nov. 26, challenging the city's designation of the former Sears site (400 block of Main Street) as an 'area in need of redevelopment with condemnation.' Owners argue the property is economically viable, was wrongly deemed blighted based mainly on vacancy since 2020, that required notice procedures weren't followed, and that using eminent domain here violates the NJ and US constitutions; the suit also references a planned sale of the property to Russo Acquisitions LLC. This is a genuine commercial-property eminent domain/condemnation dispute between a city and commercial owners, not already in js/data.js (checked: no match for Hackensack/Arcolo/Sugensteve). CAVEAT FOR THE NEWSROOM: I could not confirm from search snippets alone whether 'Nov. 26' in the source is 2026 (today) or 2025 -- other coverage references a Feb. 2026(?) council resolution and a March 2025-dated redevelopment plan as preceding events, which is consistent with either year; please open the Daily Voice/AOL article directly to confirm the byline/publish date before treating this as this week's news. There is also a long prior history on this same property (2014 NJ Supreme Court eminent domain appeal, 2022-2023 Transform/ground-lease settlement litigation) that is a separate, older dispute -- the current lead is specifically the new Nov. 26 complaint against the city's condemnation designation.

leads.title: Culver City Mall, LLC, et al. v. Wang (Westfield-Affiliated Mall Landlords Win Affirmance of $716,288.16 Judgment Against Former Burger King Franchisee)
leads.why: Primary-source read of the full opinion text (ops/opinion-leads.json key 11072393), a November 25, 2026 unpublished California Court of Appeal (Second District, Division Two) decision, case No. B344210, Los Angeles County Super. Ct. No. 22STCV38061. Plaintiffs/respondents Culver City Mall, LLC, Valencia Town Center Venture, L.P., and Plaza Bonita LLC -- all entities affiliated with Westfield, LLC -- sued Steve and Dinah Wang for breach of three mall restaurant leases (Burger King locations) after the Wangs stopped paying rent and vacated the premises (Valencia Jan. 16, 2022; Culver City June 7, 2022; Plaza Bonita June 30, 2022). The trial court granted summary judgment for the landlords in Feb. 2025 for $716,288.16 total ($356,281.27 to Culver City, $166,716.21 to Valencia, $193,290.68 to Plaza Bonita), rejecting the Wangs' forgery/authentication challenges to the leases and lease assignments; the Court of Appeal affirmed de novo on Nov. 25, 2026. Not already in js/data.js (checked for Culver City Mall/Westfield/Wang -- no match). Commercial lease dispute between mall landlords and a commercial tenant, squarely CRE and on point for the lease-disputes category; no further press coverage located or needed since the opinion itself states all facts and figures. Note for the newsroom: this is an unpublished/non-citable opinion under Cal. Rules of Court 8.1115 -- still reportable as news of what the court did, just flag that it has no precedential value.

leads.title: Carver Federal Savings Bank v. 2181 Pacific Street Housing Development Fund Corporation, Inc. (NY Appellate Division Affirms Summary Judgment in Commercial Mortgage Foreclosure, Rejects Shareholders' Unauthorized-Signatory Defense)
leads.why: Primary-source read of the full opinion text (ops/opinion-leads.json key 11072459), a November 25, 2026 decision of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of New York, Second Department (2025-07886, Index No. 505619/24), affirming Supreme Court, Kings County (Lawrence Knipel, J.), order dated May 21, 2025. The opinion states this is 'an action to foreclose a commercial mortgage encumbering certain real property located in Brooklyn,' owned by defendant 2181 Pacific Street Housing Development Fund Corporation, Inc. (HDFC). Plaintiff Carver Federal Savings Bank alleged HDFC defaulted on loan documents executed by Amina Emanuel as HDFC's Vice President. Intervenors Michael Findley, Allan Newby, Fernando Delacruz and Benjamin Salters (individually and derivatively on behalf of HDFC) argued the mortgage was invalid because Emanuel lacked authority to sign, and separately that a temporary receiver appointed for HDFC in a related action was a necessary party. The Appellate Division affirmed summary judgment for the bank on both points. Not already in js/data.js (checked for Carver Federal Savings Bank/2181 Pacific/HDFC -- no match). This is a genuine commercial-mortgage foreclosure/lending-foreclosure matter; no amount/damages figure is stated in the opinion excerpt, and no judge is named for whom to build a profile (the panel is listed, not a single presiding judge) -- newsroom can flag if the full opinion names one once opened directly.

leads.title: Global Tradings, LLC v. Lofton Enterprise Group, LLC (Delaware Superior Court Grants Writ of Possession, Holds Unrecorded Commercial Lease Extinguished by Foreclosure Sheriff's Sale)
leads.why: Primary-source read of the full opinion text (ops/opinion-leads.json key 11072632), a November 24, 2026 memorandum opinion of the Superior Court of Delaware (Brennan, J.), Civ. Act. No. N25C-10-238 DJB, deciding Plaintiff Global Tradings, LLC's motion for writ of possession in an ejectment action against Defendant Lofton Enterprise Group, LLC over commercial property at 2 S. Congress St., Port Penn, DE. Facts per the opinion: Lofton executed an unrecorded commercial lease with the property's then-owner, Port Penn Fire Company, in December 2022; the property was later sold to IBR Properties, LLC, which took out a mortgage with Wilmington Savings Fund Society (WSFS) in March 2023; WSFS filed a foreclosure action against IBR on December 27, 2024 after default, obtaining a default judgment February 7, 2025; Global Tradings purchased the property at the resulting Sheriff's sale on July 9, 2025 and declined to execute a new lease with Lofton, then filed this ejectment action October 23, 2025. The court held that because Delaware is a race-recording jurisdiction, Lofton's unrecorded lease -- even though it predated the foreclosed mortgage -- was extinguished by the Sheriff's sale, and granted Global Tradings' motion for writ of possession. Genuine commercial lease/foreclosure/ejectment dispute between two LLCs, squarely CRE (lease-disputes and/or lending-foreclosure category). Not already in js/data.js or elsewhere in this file (checked: no match for 'Global Tradings' or 'Lofton Enterprise'). No further press coverage located or needed since the opinion itself states all facts and the procedural history (briefing and argument ran February-August 2026 before the November 24, 2026 decision).
